aboutWhatItDoes: HealthYarn lets you ask common health questions in Yorùbá, Nigerian Pidgin, or English and listen to pre-approved general health information in a natural Nigerian voice. It never generates medical advice with AI at runtime.
aboutWhatItDoesNot: HealthYarn does not diagnose illness, prescribe medicines, or calculate personal dosages. In any emergency or danger sign, go straight to a clinic.
aboutPrivacySummary: No accounts for public users. No third-party trackers. Voice clips are processed in memory and discarded immediately.
sttFailedMessage: Could not hear clearly or reach voice service. Please browse a topic below or try again.
heroEyebrow: Make we yarn about your health
heroHeadline: Ask in your language. Hear an answer you can trust.
heroSubheadline: HealthYarn answers everyday health questions out loud, in Yoruba, Pidgin or English. No reading. No typing. A health professional has checked every answer.
mockupQuestion: How do I mix ORS for running stomach?
topicOrs: Running stomach in children and ORS
problemHeading: Health advice shouldn't need good English.
problemBody: Doctors are few and always busy. Leaflets and medicine labels are in English. So many people wait too long, take medicine the wrong way, or follow what the neighbour said. HealthYarn gives everyone someone to ask.
stat3Label: is a common wait to see a doctor
howHeading: As easy as sending a voice note.
step1Body: Tap Yoruba, Pidgin or English. The app talks you through it.
step2Body: Hold the microphone and say your question, like "My child has been stooling since yesterday. What should I do?" Or just tap a picture.
step3Body: A natural Nigerian voice answers in your language. Replay it or slow it down whenever you like.
safetyBody: HealthYarn never makes up medical advice. Each answer is written from World Health Organization and Federal Ministry of Health guidance, checked by a health professional, translated, then checked again by a native speaker. If the app is not sure what you asked, it says so.
safetyBodyUnreviewed: In this preview build, the voice guidance flow is active while clinical and language review sign-off is flagged as under review.
safetyWill1: explain common health problems in simple words
safetyWill2: tell you when to go to a clinic urgently
safetyWill3: explain how to take medicines safely
safetyWillNot3: replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist
dangerCalloutBody: If what you describe sounds serious, HealthYarn stops and tells you to go to a health facility now, and shows clinics near you.
topicsBandHeading: What you can ask about today.
languagesBody: The voices are made with Spitch for Nigerian languages. Tap to hear the same answer in each language.
privacyHeading: What you say stays with you.
privacyPoint1Body: No sign-up, no name, no phone number.
privacyPoint2Body: Your voice is used to understand your question, then deleted.
privacyPoint3Body: We only count which topics people ask about, so we can improve.
partnersHeading: Working in a clinic, pharmacy or community programme?
partnersBody: Use HealthYarn to explain things to patients in their own language, or help us review and add new answers.
faq1A: No. It gives general health information that health professionals have checked. It does not examine you or diagnose you. If you feel very unwell, go to a clinic.
faq2A: It is free to use. It uses a small amount of data, and answers you have already heard work without internet.
faq3Q: Do I need to read or type?
faq3A: No. You can do everything by talking, listening and tapping pictures.
faq4A: No. Your recording is used to understand your question and is then deleted.
faq5A: Yoruba, Nigerian Pidgin and English. More are planned.
faq6Q: What if it does not understand me?
faq6A: It will tell you, and show a few questions to choose from. It will not guess.
closingHeading: Make we yarn about your health.
closingSub: Ask your first question now. It takes ten seconds.
footerDisclaimer: HealthYarn gives general health information only. It is not a substitute for a doctor, nurse or pharmacist. In an emergency, go to the nearest health facility.
footerCredits: Voices by Spitch. Built for the NCS IT Development Contest 2026.
